title: One Type or Two? Four Ways to Count

scenes.tts: An analysis draws a group around some cells. Is it one type, or two?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Type or Two? Four Ways to Count. A cloud of dots with a dashed outline around it. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: An analysis draws a group around some cells. Is it one type, or two?

scenes.tts: Recall the idea. A real type usually spaces its cells out in its own mosaic.
scenes.visual: Reminder card: one type, one mosaic, one map.
scenes.narration: Recall the idea. A real type usually spaces its cells out in its own mosaic.

scenes.tts: Here is one type. Its cells keep their distance, and its arbors overlap.
scenes.visual: A regular gold mosaic seen from above, each dot with a translucent arbor disc. A counter reads arbors per point: about 4 (illustrative).
scenes.narration: Here is one type. Its cells keep their distance, and its arbors overlap.

scenes.tts: The coverage factor is the number of arbors over an average point.
scenes.visual: On screen: coverage factor = cell density × mean dendritic field area.
scenes.narration: The coverage factor is the number of arbors over an average point.

scenes.tts: Now pour in a second type, placed independently. Colour every cell the same.
scenes.visual: A second regular mosaic drops onto the first; then all dots turn one colour, as if they were one type.
scenes.narration: Now pour in a second type, placed independently. Colour every cell the same.

scenes.tts: Predict. Treated as one type, what happens to the spacing, and to the coverage?
scenes.visual: Pause card: one type or two? Predict spacing and coverage.
scenes.narration: Predict. Treated as one type, what happens to the spacing, and to the coverage?

scenes.tts: The spacing usually turns patchy. A cell of one type can sit right beside a cell of the other.
scenes.visual: Pairs of almost touching dots are circled. Label: spacing less regular.
scenes.narration: The spacing usually turns patchy. A cell of one type can sit right beside a cell of the other.

scenes.tts: And the coverage adds up, so it reads higher than either type's own.
scenes.visual: The counter now reads about 8 (illustrative), twice the single-type value because the two types match.
scenes.narration: And the coverage adds up, so it reads higher than either type's own.

scenes.tts: So an unusually high coverage can be a sign that two types were merged.
scenes.visual: Text: high coverage can be a sign of a merge (Bae and colleagues, 2018).
scenes.narration: So an unusually high coverage can be a sign that two types were merged.

scenes.tts: But some real types are only weakly regular. A mosaic is strong support, not a strict rule.
scenes.visual: A loosely spaced mosaic labelled: weakly regular, still one type.
scenes.narration: But some real types are only weakly regular. A mosaic is strong support, not a strict rule.

scenes.tts: Each census method tests a different part of the rule.
scenes.visual: Four lenses, four separate studies, labelled: response, expression, response plus RNA or shape in one cell, shape.
scenes.narration: Each census method tests a different part of the rule.

scenes.tts: Imaging grouped cells by light response, and found at least thirty two types.
scenes.caption: Imaging grouped cells by light response, and found at least 32 types.
scenes.visual: Lens 1 lights up. Count appears: at least 32 functional types (Baden and colleagues, 2016).
scenes.narration: Imaging grouped cells by light response, and found at least 32 types.

scenes.tts: R N A sequencing grouped cells by gene expression, and ended with forty six.
scenes.caption: RNA sequencing grouped cells by gene expression, and ended with 46.
scenes.visual: Lens 2 lights up. Count appears: 46 types, from 45 clusters with one split (Tran and colleagues, 2019).
scenes.narration: RNA sequencing grouped cells by gene expression, and ended with 46.

scenes.tts: One cluster held two direction-selective types already known from function. Clustering alone had missed them.
scenes.visual: One RNA cluster splits into two, each matched to a known direction-selective type.
scenes.narration: One cluster held two direction-selective types already known from function. Clustering alone had missed them.

scenes.tts: Another team recorded spikes and found forty two functional types. For some cells, they also read that same cell's R N A or shape.
scenes.caption: Another team recorded spikes and found 42 functional types. For some cells, they also read that same cell's RNA or shape.
scenes.visual: Lens 3 lights up: a pipette on one cell, then a branch to RNA or to shape, labelled subsets. Count: 42 functional types (Goetz and colleagues, 2022).
scenes.narration: Another team recorded spikes and found 42 functional types. For some cells, they also read that same cell's RNA or shape.

scenes.tts: There, three sustained on direction-selective types shared one R N A cluster, called C ten.
scenes.caption: There, three sustained ON direction-selective types shared one RNA cluster, called C10.
scenes.visual: Three response classes with different preferred directions point to a single cluster labelled C10.
scenes.narration: There, three sustained ON direction-selective types shared one RNA cluster, called C10.

scenes.tts: Electron microscopy of one small patch supported at least thirty five types.
scenes.caption: Electron microscopy of one small patch supported at least 35 types.
scenes.visual: Lens 4 lights up over a small patch. Count: 47 anatomical clusters, at least 35 types (Bae and colleagues, 2018).
scenes.narration: Electron microscopy of one small patch supported at least 35 types.

scenes.tts: These are not rival answers. Each reflects a method, a preparation and a resolution.
scenes.visual: The four counts side by side: 32+, 46, 42, 35+. Label: not rival answers. Small text: authors read them as converging on about 45 types.
scenes.narration: These are not rival answers. Each reflects a method, a preparation and a resolution.

scenes.tts: The most trustworthy types are the ones that more than one method finds.
scenes.visual: Lines join the same type found through two or more lenses; those types glow.
scenes.narration: The most trustworthy types are the ones that more than one method finds.

scenes.tts: A primate needs its own census. In the macaque fovea, one red or green sensitive cone feeds its own midget bipolar cells.
scenes.visual: A macaque fovea packed with cones; one L or M cone connects to its own ON and OFF midget bipolar cells, then to midget ganglion cells one to one. Labels: receptive-field centre pathway; a faint schematic surround of neighbouring cones.
scenes.narration: A primate needs its own census. In the macaque fovea, one red or green sensitive cone feeds its own midget bipolar cells.

scenes.tts: That private centre keeps fine spatial detail. Midget clusters made up about eighty five percent of sampled foveal ganglion cells.
scenes.caption: That private centre keeps fine spatial detail. Midget clusters made up about 85% of sampled foveal ganglion cells.
scenes.visual: Pie chart of sampled foveal ganglion cells: midget about 85%, parasol 11%, other about 4% (Peng and colleagues, 2019).
scenes.narration: That private centre keeps fine spatial detail. Midget clusters made up about 85% of sampled foveal ganglion cells.

scenes.tts: Shared ancestry with mouse cells does not mean a shared size, frequency or job.
scenes.visual: A mouse alpha cell beside a macaque midget cell, joined by a dashed line labelled counterpart (Hahn and colleagues, 2023).
scenes.narration: Shared ancestry with mouse cells does not mean a shared size, frequency or job.

scenes.tts: Combine the evidence. A separate mosaic strengthens the case for a type, but it is not required.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: response, shape and expression together; a mosaic adds support. Four lenses, four separate studies.
scenes.narration: Combine the evidence. A separate mosaic strengthens the case for a type, but it is not required.
